biography.currentRole: Georgia State Representative, District 97 (Duluth/Gwinnett County, January 2023–present)
priorRoles: Field Organizer, Georgia Muslim Voter Project
Co-founder, Georgia Volunteer Hub (2020) — trained thousands of volunteers for Georgia Senate runoff
biography.education: B.A., Oglethorpe University; M.P.P., Georgetown University McCourt School of Public Policy (2019)
biography.background: Born June 14, 1993 in Jordan to a Palestinian family; immigrated to the US at age 7. First Palestinian-American and first Muslim woman elected to the Georgia House of Representatives. Deep community-organizing background; active in Georgia civic engagement since 2014. Won District 97 (Duluth-area, Gwinnett County) in 2022 and re-elected 2024.

campaignWebsite.notes: WebFetch unavailable; positions reconstructed from news coverage, interviews, and public statements.

statedPositions.quote: I want to be governor of Georgia so that we can raise the minimum wage, feed hungry kids, reopen hospitals, invest in small businesses, and take homes back from corporations.
statedPositions.notes: Central, repeated campaign commitment. Georgia minimum wage has not been raised since 1997 (still at federal $7.25 floor). Romman explicitly noted she was seven years old the last time it was raised.

statedPositions.quote: Expanding Medicaid coverage to spur the reopening of rural hospitals
statedPositions.notes: Medicaid expansion is a top-three stated priority. Also phrased as 'subsid[izing] access to health care to make Georgia's relatively young workforce even more attractive to employers' (Decaturish/Chamblee forum, Feb 2026). Georgia is one of the remaining non-expansion states.

statedPositions.quote: Limiting corporate home buying to make rent and homeownership more affordable; take homes back from corporations
statedPositions.notes: Specific policy: force corporations to divest single-family homes they have purchased. Framed as anti-corporate-landlord populism. Also introduced Georgia House legislation on this topic.

statedPositions.quote: Restoring access to abortions and life-saving care
statedPositions.notes: Explicit commitment to restore abortion access; has stated she would veto any bill restricting reproductive healthcare. 2022 endorsement by NARAL confirms prior record. Georgia's 6-week abortion ban (LIFE Act, 2022) creates urgency for this commitment.

statedPositions.quote: I would absolutely veto every bill that comes to my desk that targets minority groups of people. I would not support any bill that targets the rights of trans adults or kids.
statedPositions.notes: Direct quote from The Advocate interview. Drew explicit parallels between anti-Muslim scapegoating post-9/11 and current anti-transgender legislation.

statedPositions.quote: I would start with working to repeal House Bill 1105. Immigration is a federal issue, but there are state issues we can pursue.
statedPositions.notes: HB 1105 is the Georgia Criminal Alien Track and Report Act (2024), which requires local agencies to enforce immigration law and bans sanctuary policies. Romman explicitly opposed and wants to repeal it. Also criticized ICE detention as 'financially lucrative for billionaire benefactors' rather than actual deportation.

statedPositions.quote: Protecting workers, increasing apprenticeship programs, empowering small businesses to thrive, and providing childcare support
statedPositions.notes: Small business investment paired with anti-corporate populism — contrast with large corporate landlords and big tech (data centers). Policy details remain general.

statedPositions.quote: Before we permanently alter the landscape of our state, we have an obligation to properly regulate and assess both the benefits and impacts of these data centers on our communities.
statedPositions.notes: Direct legislative action: introduced HB 1012 (Georgia 2025-26 session), a bipartisan bill placing a moratorium on new data center construction until March 1, 2027. Republican Rep. Jordan Ridley co-signed. Bill in House Committee on Government Affairs as of Feb 2026.

statedPositions.quote: Republicans have controlled the state for over 20 years, and in that time, schools have been ranked lower in education and hospitals have shut down.
statedPositions.notes: Frame is critique of Republican governance on education outcomes; no specific school funding formula or school choice position stated explicitly in available sources. General support for public schools implied.

statedPositions.quote: If you want to make things actually equal, then you need to be able to make sure that everyone is on the same playing field.
statedPositions.notes: Statement made in response to Georgia Republican legislation stripping state funding from schools with diversity programs. Supports DEI; no specific policy framework articulated.

statedPositions.quote: I think when you look at the campaigns that have been run in the state, [Democrats] have actually tried to run them more to the center and to the right. And right now what people are looking for is not left versus right, they're looking for top versus bottom.
statedPositions.notes: Core strategic positioning: economic populism, class-based framing. Cites Moody's Analytics (Mark Zandi) data that Georgia is already in recession. Explicit rejection of centrist Democratic triangulation.
Recurring campaign slogan element but policy detail (school meals? SNAP? WIC?) not yet specified in available sources.

keyBills.status: In House Committee on Government Affairs as of Feb 2026
keyBills.notes: Would prohibit local governments from issuing permits for new data centers through March 1, 2027. Bipartisan bill (Republican co-signer: Rep. Jordan Ridley of Woodstock). Romman criticized competing HB 1063 as lacking consumer protections.

keyBills.bill: EMS Essential Service Designation Bill (reintroduced 2025-26 session)
keyBills.status: Reintroduced after failing in prior session due to time
keyBills.notes: Would designate Emergency Medical Services as an essential service in Georgia, enabling EMS providers to access grants. Bipartisan (Republican Rep. Gary Richardson co-working). 14 other states already have this designation.

keyBills.bill: Corporate Home Buying / Anti-Corporate Landlord Bill
keyBills.status: Introduced in prior session; details of current-session status unclear
keyBills.notes: Legislation to force corporations to divest single-family homes. Specifically targets institutional investors buying up residential housing stock.
Bring back the office responsible for protecting consumers (office had been eliminated or defunded). Details limited in available public records.

keyBills.bill: HB 1105 — Georgia Criminal Alien Track and Report Act (2024)
keyBills.status: Passed; signed by Gov. Kemp May 1, 2024
keyBills.notes: Romman explicitly stated she would work to repeal this law as governor. Bill requires local agencies to enforce federal immigration law, expands ban on sanctuary policies, criminalizes officials who fail to comply. Romman opposed as anti-immigrant overreach.

votingRecord.notes: As a minority-party state legislator in a Republican-dominated Georgia House, Romman's voting record is largely defined by opposition votes and sponsored minority bills that rarely pass. Evidence of her positions comes more reliably from her sponsored legislation, committee work, and public statements than from consequential floor votes. Georgia does not appear to publish individual roll-call vote data in an easily searchable online format for this researcher layer.

foreignPolicyNote.summary: Romman is Palestinian-American and has been the most prominent elected Palestinian American voice on the Gaza conflict. She was selected by the Uncommitted Movement to deliver a speech at the 2024 DNC; the DNC refused to allow her on stage. She delivered the speech outside, calling for a ceasefire and endorsing Kamala Harris. Her proposed speech would NOT have called for an arms embargo — a notable moderation from the Uncommitted platform. She endorsed Harris.
foreignPolicyNote.dnc_quote: Let's commit to each other, to electing Vice President Harris and defeating Donald Trump who uses my identity as a Palestinian as a slur.
foreignPolicyNote.relevanceNote: Foreign policy is not a governor's domain, but Romman's Palestinian-American identity and Gaza advocacy are major factors in her national profile and primary electability calculus. Some Democratic primary voters may see this as a liability; progressive Arab/Muslim voters see it as a key credential.

primaryRaceContext.pollingPosition: Not registering significant poll numbers in available polling (Bottoms at 40%, Thurmond 11%, Duncan 5%, Esteves 3% in AJC poll — others not listed). Romman is a lower-tier candidate by fundraising and polling metrics.
primaryRaceContext.campaignDistinction: Running explicitly to the left of the field; Project 159 grassroots organizing strategy (volunteers in all 159 Georgia counties); economic populist framing contrasted with 'centrist' Democratic strategy failures

positionConflicts.conflict: Romman is closely identified with the pro-Palestine Uncommitted movement, but her DNC speech would not have called for an arms embargo — a key Uncommitted demand. She also ultimately endorsed Harris. This creates a tension between her identity as a Palestinian-American advocate and her practical choices within Democratic party politics.

evidenceSummary.notes: Three-year state House record (minority party) provides legislative direction but limited consequential votes. Campaign platform is explicit on 5-6 axes; several axes have no available evidence. As a state-office race, some federal-level axes (firearms federal legislation, federal immigration) are less directly applicable but state-level analogs exist. Her Palestinian identity and Uncommitted movement association are the dominant narrative frame in most news coverage, which has somewhat crowded out detailed policy reporting on other domestic axes. Primary polling suggests she is not a frontrunner, which may limit detailed platform development in available public sources.
